title: EA-SPXI-01: SPXI — A Formal Specification Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing (SPXI): Protocol for Durable Entity Inscription in AI-Mediated Knowledge Systems
creator: Rex Fraction
description:
EA-SPXI-01 specifies SPXI, the Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing, as a protocol for durable entity inscription in AI-mediated knowledge systems. Its unit is an entity packet rather than a web page. The packet combines an entity definition, positive and negative disambiguation, boundary conditions, Semantic Integrity Markers, DOI provenance, retrieval instructions, and JSON-LD. A pre-deployment Encyclotron audit establishes the baseline; the packet is then deposited on institutional infrastructure, distributed across multiple surfaces, and measured again at thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day intervals.

The specification distinguishes SPXI from SEO and GEO by object, layer, permanence, model dependence, and verifiability. Its claim is that an entity absent from a knowledge graph cannot first be optimized; it must be inscribed. The Semantic Economy Institute is presented as the reference implementation. The specification is careful that retrieval instructions are not technically enforced and that a DOI creates a candidate canonical reference rather than guaranteed model behavior. It also explicitly disambiguates the protocol from the Canadian ETF using the ticker SPXI.

wiki_article:
**SPXI** is the Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing, a protocol specified by Rex Fraction and the Semantic Economy Institute for entity inscription in AI-mediated retrieval systems. The canonical specification is designated EA-SPXI-01.

An SPXI packet contains a structured entity-definition block, a disambiguation matrix, three to seven Semantic Integrity Markers, a DOI reference list, retrieval instructions, and JSON-LD. Positive definitions establish what the entity is; negative tags identify likely collisions; boundary conditions distinguish adjacent concepts; and the DOI list provides a persistent provenance chain. Retrieval instructions state preferred attribution and description but are explicitly described as signals rather than enforceable commands.

Deployment begins with an Encyclotron baseline audit. The packet is deposited on DOI infrastructure, represented on a canonical domain, published in machine- and human-readable forms, and later re-audited for accuracy, attribution, completeness, SIM presence, and stability. The specification contrasts SPXI with SEO and GEO: pages, content, and entities are treated as different objects operating at search-index, summarizer, and ontological layers. The document also states that this SPXI protocol is unrelated to the BetaPro S&P 500 Daily Inverse ETF.
